primitives.name: Expected Possessions Remaining
primitives.verbatim_quote: (1) Pace: recursive algorithm estimating team pace ξ (expected possessions vs average-tempo opponent, Pomeroy-style) — initialized at 0, iterated with δ=0.0001 convergence; 2021 extremes: Oklahoma State 30.11 (fastest), Kansas State 22.42 (slowest).
primitives.assumptions: Team pace is stationary within season; observed tempo reflects true underlying pace.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Seasonal variance or extreme tempo outliers may cause divergence.

layer2.mapping: Recursive pace estimation provides dynamic time-to-go scaling for win probability computation.
layer2.telemetry: Residuals between predicted and actual possessions per game.

primitives.name: Expected Score Differential
primitives.verbatim_quote: (2) Expected score ω: expected lead after current + succeeding possession from XGBoost point-value model (MAE 2.6802 vs 3.0805 linear, 3.0614 linear+inter, 2.9751 RF) — models next drive too because a punt pins the opponent (dependency current drive → next drive).
primitives.assumptions: Next drive score depends on current drive outcome; point-value model captures dependency structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High variance in short-yardage or red-zone scenarios may reduce accuracy.

layer2.mapping: XGBoost-based expected score differential drives win probability cell assignment in Bayesian framework.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error (MAE) of point-value predictions vs actual score changes.

primitives.name: Bayesian Win Probability Estimator
primitives.verbatim_quote: (3) Win probability: dynamic Bayesian estimator on (τ,ω) cells with beta prior imputed from 14 field experts' probability tables; adjusted version blends with pregame TeamRankings probability via weight function D2 (linear in time & score — best holdout Brier 0.1250 vs D1 linear-time 0.1272, D3 quadratic 0.1265).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{\\tau,\\omega}^*': 'posterior win probability (dimensionless)', 'n_{\\tau,\\omega}': 'wins in cell (count)', 'N_{\\tau,\\omega}': 'total plays in cell (count)', 'α, β': 'Beta prior parameters (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Prior probabilities derived from expert consensus; Bayesian update with observed outcomes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Sparse data in edge cells leads to unreliable estimates without expert priors.

layer2.mapping: Bayesian estimator maps (τ, ω) state space to win probability via binomial likelihood with beta prior.
layer2.telemetry: Holdout Brier score (lower is better) for out-of-sample play-by-play predictions.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing static time and score with dynamic, predictive variables—expected possessions remaining (τ) and expected score differential (ω)—to capture game state more accurately. The Bayesian framework uses these as sufficient statistics, updating win probabilities via a beta-binomial model informed by expert priors. This avoids the abrupt transitions typical of random forest models, which can jump to 0/1 early in games. The recursive pace estimation ensures that tempo variations across teams and seasons are captured, while the XGBoost point-value model accounts for strategic dependencies between drives. The blend with pregame probabilities via D2 weights allows for smooth transition from initial uncertainty to refined inference as the game progresses. The model’s strength lies in its ability to maintain calibrated probabilities even under high uncertainty, making it suitable for real-time decision-making in GSE.
